First, we complete the square:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =-{x}^{2}+22x-21 \\  & =-({x}^{2}-22x)-21 \\  & =-({x}^{2}-2\cdot 11x+{11}^{2}-{11}^{2})-21 \\  & =-((x-11)^{2}-121)-21 \\  & =-(x-11)^{2}+121-21 \\  & =-(x-11)^{2}+100\end{aligned}
$$

    

To find the inverse of a function, we follow these steps:

**Step 1:** Replace $f(x)$ with $y$:

$$
y=-(x-11)^{2}+100
$$

**Step 2:** Swap $x$ and $y$:

$$
x=-(y-11)^{2}+100
$$

**Step 3:** Solve for $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-(y-11)^{2}+100 \\ x-100 & =-(y-11)^{2} \\ 100-x & =(y-11)^{2} \\ \sqrt{100-x} & =y-11 \\ \sqrt{100-x}+11 & =y\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we selected the positive square root because if $x\ge 11$ is the domain of $f,$ then the range of the inverse is ${f}^{-1}\ge 11.$

**Step 4:** Replace $y$ with ${f}^{-1}(x)$:

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\sqrt{100-x}+11
$$
